subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept the one-way PortGuardian JSON-to-SQLite cutover, including blocking mixed JSON-writing app copies and no supported rollback to a JSON-only build after migration?
rationale: This is an intentional upgrade and recovery-policy change affecting host-global tunnel ownership; code review cannot choose the supported downgrade and mixed-version contract on maintainers’ behalf.

options.title: Accept the staged one-way cutover
options.body: Land the prerequisite and this PR after final-head native proof confirms the documented migration and recovery behavior.

options.title: Require a backward-compatible transition
options.body: Keep old JSON-only copies interoperable, which would require a different migration and ownership design before merge.

options.title: Defer the migration
options.body: Keep the JSON ledger until maintainers choose a supported multi-version upgrade policy.

recommendation.title: Accept the staged one-way cutover
recommendation.body: Land the prerequisite and this PR after final-head native proof confirms the documented migration and recovery behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the connected native-state and PortGuardian migration stack and documented the proposed compatibility contract.
